item.title: Metalens microscope switches focus with voltage, not moving optics
item.description: Just as it is difficult for a camera to keep both a nearby flower and a distant mountain sharply focused at the same time, conventional optical microscopes face a similar challenge when imaging structures located at different depths inside the body. Tighter focusing of light improves spatial resolution, but at the same time reduces the depth range over which the image remains sharply focused.

item.title: Single optical element combines soft X-ray imaging and spectroscopy
item.description: An international research team from Germany, Switzerland and Japan has demonstrated in a recent study that a single reflection zone plate (RZP) can perform both soft X-ray imaging and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) mapping. The approach could simplify future instruments that need to determine both where structures are located in a material and how their electronic properties vary.

item.title: Counting magnetic flux quanta offers new way to measure photon numbers
item.description: Researchers at AIST have directly observed magnetic flux quanta generated in a superconductor by photon absorption and demonstrated a new principle of photon detection that identifies the number of photons based on the number of these flux quanta.

item.title: Light-based method enables precise control of ultrafast electron flow in a scanning tunneling microscope
item.description: What would it take to watch an electron move through a material? Researchers would need to see individual atoms and capture an electron's motion at incredibly short timescales. A Technion-led team has brought those two capabilities together in a scanning tunneling microscope, using carefully shaped laser pulses to control the direction of electron flow while preserving nanoscale spatial resolution.

item.title: Ultrafast light pulses track molecular motion with three-femtosecond resolution
item.description: Researchers have observed a molecule in the first instants after it has absorbed light and tracked the coordinated motion of electrons and nuclei with a temporal resolution of three femtoseconds. This is the result achieved by an international research group led by the Politecnico di Milano, which has developed a new apparatus for studying ultrafast photochemical processes.

item.title: Ultrafast light can control ferromagnetism without relying on heating
item.description: Despite being known for more mundane uses such as sticking notes to refrigerators or keeping bags shut, magnetization is one of the most fundamental and useful properties of a material. Indeed, it forms the physical basis for storing most of our digital information, encoding the bits used in hard drives, computer memories and credit cards.

item.title: Sapphire-grown semiconductor film sets bandgap record
item.description: Semiconductors with wider bandgaps could pave the way for smaller, more efficient electronics that can handle far higher voltages, but the wider this gap becomes, the harder it is to control how well a material conducts electricity. Now, a team led by Darrell Schlom at Cornell University has shown that adding silicon to thin films of aluminum gallium oxide can keep this control intact at bandgaps wider than any semiconductor before it. Their research has been published in Nature.

item.title: X-ray free-electron laser sets new record for shortest high-energy pulses
item.description: Researchers at the Linac Coherent Light Source (LCLS) at the U.S. Department of Energy's SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory have measured the shortest high-energy X-ray pulses ever recorded at an X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL). The pulses had photon energies of about 9 kiloelectronvolts (keV) and clocked in at durations of 100 to 400 attoseconds—mere billionths of a billionth of a second. The results are published in Nature Photonics.

item.title: Physicists reveal new paradigm for fiber growth in neurodegenerative diseases
item.description: Some proteins that are linked to neurodegenerative diseases can form both liquid droplets and amyloid fibers. But how are these two states connected, and where do the fibers grow? Leiden physicists Liru Feng and Louise Jawerth have discovered a counter-intuitive mechanism.

item.title: Tiny shifts in iron content tip a potential memory material between competing magnetic states
item.description: A team of Yale researchers has figured out what gives a magnetic material its mysterious properties, a discovery that could help boost computing memory and the field of "spintronics." Their work is published in Physical Review Letters.

item.title: One extra quantum dot helps balance speed and stability in spin qubits
item.description: Quantum computers need qubits that can be controlled both quickly and reliably. Yet making semiconductor spin qubits faster often makes them more sensitive to electrical noise, creating a difficult trade-off.

item.title: How Voting Is Like a Klein Bottle
item.description: A new topological model connects a centuries-old voting paradox to a surface with no distinct inside or outside. The post How Voting Is Like a Klein Bottle first appeared on Quanta Magazine

item.title: Patterns of polar vortices discovered in lead-free superlattices on silicon
item.description: A team at HZB has, for the first time, reported polar vortices in (BaTiO₃/SrTiO₃)₁₀ superlattices on silicon. These results expand the range of materials and substrates on which polar topological textures can occur and open up new options for incorporating complex ferroelectric states into silicon-based technologies.

item.title: 相比黑猩猩，人类为什么更容易患上骨关节炎？
item.description: 一项基因组学研究表明，人类关节软骨中关键缓冲成分硫酸化糖胺聚糖（sGAG）的含量仅为黑猩猩等类人猿的约三分之一。这种在演化过程中出现的基因表达下调与软骨成分改变，虽然塑造了人类独特的骨骼形态，但也可能使人类更容易患上骨关节炎等退行性骨骼疾病。

item.title: Plain silicon grating reveals a hidden 'twist' in light from electron beams
item.description: In 1953, two physicists showed that an electron beam skimming past a grating emits light whose color depends only on the electron's speed and the grating's spacing. Known as Smith-Purcell radiation, this phenomenon has become a useful tool for building compact, tunable light sources and tracking particle beams without touching them.

item.title: What makes glass good at conducting heat? Sound holds the key
item.description: Glass can keep a drink safely contained, protect a smartphone screen, or serve as a foundation for electronic components. But when it comes to controlling heat, this familiar material still holds some scientific mysteries. Now, researchers have identified a key factor governing how efficiently heat travels through silicate glass, offering a new guideline for designing glass materials for next-generation electronic devices.

item.title: Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering
item.description: To invade red blood cells, the deadly protist creates a temporary molecular portal that disappears behind it — a door we can now see in fine detail. The post Malaria Parasite Caught in the Act of Breaking and Entering first appeared on Quanta Magazine

item.title: 30万至10万年前，东亚大地上的古人类可能大多是丹尼索瓦人？
item.description: 许家窑人的身份在分子层面得到确认，也让研究者第一次有机会系统认识丹尼索瓦人的形态特征。

item.description: 最近，困扰数学界30余年的三维Ghys猜想，在中国数学家与AI协作下取得突破。

item.title: 在沃森追思会上，我重新认识Jim Watson
item.description: 9月28日，在沃森追思会结束后，我和博后老板Michael Wigler餐叙闲聊，期间他讲了一句让我印象很深的话：Double helix structure also made Watson（双螺旋结构亦塑造了沃森）。

item.title: 商周新书：《巴斯德传》 ｜ 周忠和作序
item.description: 商周撰写的科学三巨人传记，孟德尔与詹纳都可以被同时冠以科学家与博物学家的头衔，而巴斯德稍有不同，更像一位真正现代意义上的科学家。

item.title: 会“隐身”的纹身来了
item.description: 美国科学家开发出一种名为 PhotoTat 的智能纹身墨水，只需经过几秒钟紫外光照射，原本隐形的图案便会迅速显现，并可以在需要时再次“消失”。

item.description: 近日，法默的新书《理解混沌：更好的经济理论，更好地理解世界》中文版出版。

item.title: AI冲击数学，信誉系统崩盘，数学界何去何从？
item.description: 10月6日，Openai一下子在网上放出722 篇文章，包含了400 个左右数学猜想的解，对数学界造成巨大的冲击。我愿意称之为“第四次数学危机”。

item.description: 2026年10月18日是杨振宁逝世一周年，《知识分子》重发此文，以纪念杨振宁先生。访谈者施郁当时是复旦大学教授，目前为中国科学技术大学教授。

item.title: 诺奖评委前主席：吴健雄漏选的遗憾
item.description: 70年前，杨振宁与李政道因提出弱相互作用中宇称不守恒的理论，获得1957年诺贝尔物理学奖。这项工作深刻影响了现代物理学的发展。

item.title: 这个科技加速时代，是人文的冬天还是春天？
item.description: 当公众最需要人文与社会科学提供意义坐标时，听到的却常常只有两种声音：困在概念里的自我循环，或是对技术的情绪化惊惧。
